{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the bottom line of the fish (stroke 2), branching it off the nose so the start feeds both body lines. That line is connected and carries the fall along the belly to the tail crossing. In the last five minutes I took on the fish's remaining open area, the notch in the tail fork. I laid the upper notch join from the fork into the pale pair, and I was laying the lower join when time was called. I can't say whether that last join closed the notch.

Execution: I picked one piece of work, the bottom line, and stayed on it until it was down and live. I inspected the notch twice to find which line ends were open before spending dominoes on it. With the pile nearly empty, I asked teammates to lift pale, disconnected strays so I had dominoes to finish the joins. I also kept my hands off other people's pieces.

Collaboration: I gave clear status updates to the whole table. I coordinated with Leo on meeting in the middle of the bottom line and on standing back up the dominoes knocked near his end. I asked Tom and Leo to stay off the notch while I was working there, so we wouldn't bump each other. I took Priya's offer of spare dominoes and her read on the two open ends, which saved me time.

Leadership: I took ownership of the notch, the last open spot, and told the table what I was doing and what I needed. I gave a clear status summary when the manager checked in. That let the others redirect their time to jams and strays instead of duplicating work.

My share: I built one of the two body lines and made the notch joins, which is a meaningful but partial part of a four-person build.", "my_share_percent": 25}
